items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: So Cannonball asked, he says, “What do you want to play?” I says, “Well play anything out of your book.”

ctx.x: You know, strange you mention that because this last week, Verve Records called me and sent me two cassettes they’re going to re-issue. They bought the catalogue I think, the old catalogue from Mercury on those sides that we did that you’re talking about and they’re going to put them out in a double CD. And they sent them to me to listen to and clarify like some of the, there were a lot of errors as far as composer credits, and that’s why they sent them to me along with the sheet with the thing on it, which I had…

you could put your civilian clothes on, on any Army post in the States (not overseas). But I’m sitting there, you know I’m walking guard duty with combat boots, helmet, cartridge belt, and so Cannonball’s giving me like such a look of disdain, I’ve never seen in my life, like wow, who is this cat? And the rest of the guys in the band are looking like, “Huh?” So Cannonball asked, he says, “What do you want to play?” I says, “Well play anything out of your book.” And by saying it like that, you know, that kind of…
Nobody was there by choice, right?

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But Cannonball used to like to play fast. Because this was right after we both got out of the Army. And we used to do that a lot. We changed drummers a lot working with Cannonball, but Jimmy Cobb could handle it.

ctx.x: Were there occasions where you’d have to say I don’t know that but tomorrow I will?

Yeah, yeah. Sometimes I’d learn it on the gig. Maybe I’d heard the tune but had never played it. They stuck pretty much to standards, plus most of them, you know I was great for listening to records in those days. Like in the Army, I was in the Army with Cannonball and we had more records than we had clothes in our barracks. We had two record players and we shared a room, because I was the Company Clerk, and Cannonball was the head of the Band Training Unit. And we had two record players to begin with, and we…
